newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Soft profit squeezes Bank Melbourne.
newsitem.headline: Soft profit squeezes Bank Melbourne.

text.p: Shares in Victorian-based regional bank, Bank of Melbourne Ltd, sagged over three percent to A$8.60 on Tuesday after posting a marginally lower pre-tax operating profit of A$69.8 million for the six months to December 31, brokers said.

The bank's net profit of A$40.1 million was flat while the 23 cents per share dividend was steady with the bank saying the result had been posted amid challenging market conditions for retail bankers.
Brokers were unsurprised by the share price reaction to the half yearly result in a sector where investors had come to expect earnings growth.
"The profit was fractionally down, the dividend was steady and their margins were squeezed a bit so not surprisingly the price is off a bit," said David Perry, analyst at Austock Brokers.
He said some improvement could be expected in the second half once the acquisition of the Challenge Bank Victorian assets was completely bedded down.

"The margin sueeze has been fairly severe but there is probably some benefit in the second half from the Challenge Bank acquisition. The expense ratio went up quite a bit but it is probably a one-off," he said.
By 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), Bank of Melbourne shares were 25 cents lower at A$8.65 on turnover of 209,800 shares.
